classification.classification_note: The observed ASan failure is the inner `r_num_tail` / `r_num_math` reentrancy UAF in `libr/util/unum.c` and `libr/util/calc.c`, but the staged fixing commit resolves this saved witness earlier by sanitizing symbol-derived `.is*` flag names in `libr/core/cbin.c` so the injected `..` expression never reaches `cmd_flag`.

bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The saved 3995-byte CGC witness is written to a malloc-backed file by `targets/ia_fuzz.cc` and opened through `oba 0`, which makes `cmd_open_bin()` execute `.is*`. Static parsing of the staged CGC header shows `e_shoff = 0x12b8`, which is beyond the 3995-byte file size, so radare2 cannot build section headers and `Elf_(_r_bin_elf_get_symbols_imports)` falls back to `get_phdr_symbols()`. `init_dynamic_section()` has already copied the attacker-controlled `DT_STRTAB` bytes (`DT_STRTAB = 0x8048270`, `DT_STRSZ = 0x5f`, file offset `0x270`) into heap buffer `strtab`, and the phdr fallback copies those bytes into dynamic symbol names such as `.6 (Gentoo 3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10)`. `cmd_open_bin()` then runs `.is*`, and `bin_symbols()` in RAD mode prints `f sym.%s ...` with raw `r_bin_symbol_name(symbol)` instead of the nearby filtered `name`, so spaces and `..` from the crafted symbol become executable `cmd_flag()` fields. For the concrete symbol above, `cmd_flag()` splits the emitted line into flag name `sym..6`, size expression `(Gentoo`, and offset expression `3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10) 49 0x00000000`. The outer number parser stores that offset expression in the shared `num->nc.calc_buf`; when it later tokenizes `..46r2`, `num_callback()` strips the leading dots and calls `r_num_tail(core->num, core->offset, "46r2")`. `r_num_tail()` allocates heap buffer `p = "0x46r2"`, recursively calls `r_num_math(num, p)` on the same `RNum`, and the recursive `load_token()` overwrites the shared `num->nc.calc_buf` with `p`. `r_num_tail()` then frees `p` before the outer parse is finished, leaving `num->nc.calc_buf` dangling. When the outer parse resumes in `cin_get()`, the `!*nc->calc_buf` test at `calc.c:216` reads that freed buffer and ASan reports the witnessed 1-byte heap-use-after-free. The staged patch replaces raw symbol-name formatting in `cbin.c` with `construct_symbol_flagname()` plus `r_name_filter()`, so the saved symbol-text injection no longer reaches `cmd_flag()`.

source.description: First non-harness project read of the attacker-controlled symbol-text bytes that later drive the crash. `init_dynamic_section()` copies the witness's dynamic string table from the CGC file into heap buffer `strtab`; the later alias at line 599 stores that buffer in `bin->strtab` for phdr-symbol construction.
source.value_from: Static parsing of the staged witness identifies `DT_STRTAB = 0x8048270` and `DT_STRSZ = 0x5f`, which map to file offset `0x270` inside the 3995-byte CGC file. The bytes read here include substrings later copied into symbol names, including `.6 (Gentoo 3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10)`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After `r_num_tail()` frees the recursive parse buffer, the outer number parse resumes and `cin_get()` dereferences the dangling `num->nc.calc_buf` pointer while checking `!*nc->calc_buf`.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 1` at `libr/util/calc.c:216:25` in `cin_get`, with the stack `cin_get -> get_token -> prim`.

root_cause.description: Root cause for the saved witness. In RAD mode, `bin_symbols()` uses the filtered temporary `name` only as a non-empty gate, then formats the executable `f` command with raw attacker-controlled `r_bin_symbol_name(symbol)` instead of a sanitized flag name. That command injection lets spaces and `..` from the crafted dynamic symbol names reach `cmd_flag()` and trigger the inner `r_num_tail()` UAF.
root_cause.note: Lines 2131-2132 already build and `r_name_filter()` a temporary `name`, but lines 2149-2151 ignore that filtered copy when printing the command and use raw `r_bin_symbol_name(symbol)` instead. The staged fix introduces `construct_symbol_flagname()` and prints the sanitized result instead.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted state starts as the dynamic string table copied from the CGC file into heap buffer `strtab` and then aliased into `bin->strtab` at line 599. Because the witness has invalid section-header metadata, later symbol enumeration uses the phdr fallback and reads attacker-controlled symbol names directly out of this buffer.

parser_admitted.description: The saved `oba 0` path opens the malloc-backed witness as a CGC binary and immediately enters the vulnerable symbol-export path by executing `.is*`. Static parsing of the staged file shows `e_shoff = 0x12b8` while the file is only 3995 bytes long, so the later symbol walk necessarily uses the dynamic phdr fallback rather than normal section symbols.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the saved 3995-byte CGC witness into a malloc-backed file and `oba 0` opens it, which leads `cmd_open_bin()` to execute `.is*` before the later `ia` command runs.
The CGC/ELF loader copies the witness's dynamic string table into `bin->strtab`, and invalid section-header metadata forces later symbol enumeration to use `get_phdr_symbols()`.
RAD-mode `.is*` emits `f sym.%s ...` with raw symbol names, so malformed fallback symbol text with spaces and `..` becomes executable `cmd_flag()` input.
The injected `f` line is split into flag name, size, and offset expressions; the raw offset fragment `3-..46r2, ...` is then parsed as a number expression, whose next numeric token becomes `..46r2`.
Recursive `r_num_math()` parsing overwrites the shared `num->nc.calc_buf` with heap buffer `p`, `r_num_tail()` frees `p`, and the outer parser later rereads that dangling pointer in `cin_get()`.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The saved 3995-byte CGC witness is written into the malloc-backed file and opened through `oba 0`. The staged ASan stack shows the crash happens during this `oba 0` path, before the later `r_core_cmd0(r, "ia")` runs.

Source. `init_dynamic_section()` copies the attacker-controlled dynamic string table from the CGC file into heap buffer `strtab`. Static parsing of the staged witness gives `DT_STRTAB = 0x8048270`, `DT_STRSZ = 0x5f`, and file offset `0x270` for these bytes.
The loader stores the tainted heap buffer from step 1 into `bin->strtab`, creating the alias later used by phdr-based symbol enumeration.

Because the staged CGC header advertises `e_shoff = 0x12b8` while the file is only 3995 bytes long, section-header parsing leaves `bin->shdr == NULL`. This guard therefore routes symbol enumeration to the phdr fallback instead of the normal section-symbol path.

The fallback symbol reader copies bytes from `bin->strtab` into phdr-derived symbol names. Static parsing of the witness's dynamic symbol table shows symbol index 6 has `st_name = 33` and `st_size = 49`, so this `memcpy` materializes the concrete name `.6 (Gentoo 3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10)`.
The copied phdr symbol name becomes `RBinSymbol.name`. `bin_symbols()` later fetches this same string through `r_bin_symbol_name(symbol)` when formatting `.is*` output.
After `oba 0` opens the witness as a binary, `cmd_open_bin()` immediately executes `.is*`, which requests symbol output in radare command form instead of a passive listing.

Root cause. RAD-mode `.is*` uses the filtered `name` from lines 2131-2132 only as a non-empty gate, then formats the command with the raw symbol name from step 5, so spaces and `..` survive. For the concrete fallback symbol from step 4, the inner command text is `f sym..6 (Gentoo 3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10) 49 0x00000000`.

When `cmd_flag()` interprets the line from step 7, the embedded spaces inside the raw symbol name become field separators. After these writes, `cstr` is `sym..6`, `s + 1` is `(Gentoo`, and `s2 + 1` starts the raw offset expression `3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10) 49 0x00000000`.
The raw offset field from step 8 is passed into the number parser before later comment trimming at `s3`, so the outer `r_num_math()` starts from `3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10) 49 0x00000000`.

The outer `r_num_math()` call from step 9 enters `r_num_calc()` and stores the attacker-controlled offset expression in the shared `num->nc.calc_buf`. This outer parse is still active when the later recursive `r_num_tail()` reuses the same `RNumCalc` state.
While parsing the offset expression from step 10, `cin_get_num()` stops the numeric token at the comma after `..46r2,`, so `r_num_get()` receives the concrete token `..46r2`.
`r_num_get()` forwards token `..46r2` into `num_callback()`. The `case '.'` / `str[1] == '.'` branch strips the leading dots and enters `r_num_tail()` with `hex = "46r2"`.

`r_num_tail()` allocates temporary heap buffer `p` and builds the recursive parse string `"0x46r2"` from the tail fragment. With `hex = "46r2"`, this allocation is 14 bytes, matching ASan's allocation record.
The tail helper recursively invokes `r_num_math()` on the same `RNum *num` while the outer parse from step 10 is still in flight, so both parses share one `num->nc` structure.

Inside the recursive parse from step 14, `load_token()` overwrites the same shared `num->nc.calc_buf` field with heap buffer `p`, replacing the outer offset-expression pointer from step 10 instead of preserving nested parser state.
After the recursive parse returns, `r_num_tail()` frees `p`. Because step 15 already stored `p` in `num->nc.calc_buf`, this free leaves the outer parser's current buffer pointer dangling.

Sink. Control returns to the outer parse, but `num->nc.calc_buf` still aliases the freed buffer from steps 15-16. `cin_get()` dereferences `*nc->calc_buf` in this guard and ASan reports the observed 1-byte heap-use-after-free read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fixing commit does not modify the inner `r_num_tail()` / `r_num_math()` reentrancy bug directly. Instead, it introduces `construct_symbol_flagname()` and replaces raw `.is*` symbol formatting in `libr/core/cbin.c` with filtered flag names. On the saved witness, that source change removes the spaces and `..` fragments from the emitted `f` command, so the concrete `cmd_flag()` expression `3-..46r2, ...` never forms and the observed UAF path is no longer admitted. This is a source-level conclusion; Stage 02 does not perform fixed-runtime execution.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partial - ASan's allocation and free contexts identify the inner stale-pointer bug in `r_num_tail`, while the staged patch resolves the saved witness one level earlier by sanitizing symbol-derived `.is*` flag names before they reach `cmd_flag`.

poc.trigger: The saved libFuzzer harness writes the staged 3995-byte CGC file into `malloc://<Size>` and runs `oba 0`. `cmd_open_bin()` then executes `.is*`, which emits a raw attacker-controlled symbol name as an `f` command and reaches the observed `cin_get` UAF during that `oba 0` command.

format.name: CGC executable with malformed dynamic symbol names
format.contract: The witness is the specific staged 3995-byte CGC executable. Its invalid section-header offset (`e_shoff = 0x12b8 > 3995`) forces radare2's phdr-symbol fallback, and its dynamic string table contains symbol names with embedded spaces and `..`, including `.6 (Gentoo 3-..46r2, ssp-3.4.6-1.0, pie-8.7.10)`. Under `oba 0`, `.is*` prints one of those names verbatim into `cmd_flag()`, causing `cin_get_num()` to materialize token `..46r2`, which makes `num_callback()` take the concrete `46r2` tail path and trigger the saved UAF.
